chunks: Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Ibn Muskan, from Muhammad al-Halabi, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:
Do not sever the spinal cord of the slaughtered animal until it dies. When it has died, then sever it.

key_terms.الذبيحة: The slaughtered/sacrificed animal; the one upon whom the slaughter has been performed
key_terms.نخع: Severing or cutting the spinal cord (nakh'a); a post-slaughter procedure that must occur after the animal is dead

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to sever the spinal cord of an animal before it dies after slaughter?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) issued a jurisprudential ruling regarding the naKh (severing of the spinal cord) of slaughtered animals. He prohibited performing this act before the animal has completely died, and permitted it only after death has occurred. This ruling relates to ensuring proper and humane slaughter according to Islamic law, as premature severing of the spinal cord could affect the validity of the slaughter and cause undue harm.

en.hubeali:
Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan, from Ibn Muskan, from Muhammad Al Halby who said, 
‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said:
‘Do not flip over the slaughter until it dies. So when it is dead, so flip it over’.
en.sarwar: 6. Abu Ali af-Ash‘ariy has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd af-Jabbar from Safwan from ibn Muskan from Muhammad af-Halabiy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Do not cut off the spinal cord of the animal you slaughter before it dies; and when it dies, then you can cut off its spinal cord.’”
